motions.summary: The council approved fencing and buffer standards, barring berms or hedges as substitutes for required fences, defining split-rail fencing, and letting the city treat unsafe fences as nuisances.
motions.impact: If your fence is falling apart, built from broken or flammable scrap, or put up to spite a neighbor, the city can now declare it a nuisance and make you fix it. Most homeowners are unaffected.

motions.headline: Mayor can't create city policy without a council vote
motions.summary: The council adopted rules barring the mayor or staff from enacting policy without a majority council vote, and requiring the council to vote on liaison assignments.
motions.impact: This is about who holds power inside city hall, not your street or your bill. New city rules now have to clear a council vote in a public meeting rather than being set by the mayor's office.

motions.headline: Council members assigned to city boards for 2024
motions.summary: The council set its 2024 board assignments: Burnham to cemetery and arts, Clark to seniors and library, Gray to veterans, parks and youth, Wood to economic development, Wright to planning.
motions.impact: This tells you which council member to contact about a given topic — Wright for planning issues, Clark for the library or senior center, Gray for parks. Nothing else changes.

motions.headline: Jared Gray named mayor pro tem
motions.summary: The council elected Councilmember Jared Gray as mayor pro tempore, the member who fills in when the mayor is unavailable.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is internal housekeeping about who steps in to run a meeting when the mayor can't be there.
